topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, the scope of the cancer lecture series, and the core learning outcomes concerning environmental carcinogens, testing methodologies, and tumor initiation versus promotion.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Cancer Development, Risk Factors, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the fundamental biology of cancer as a genetic and microenvironmental disease, the relative roles of endogenous errors versus environmental exposures, and global epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens and Viral Oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious agents such as bacteria, parasites, and viruses contribute to cancer development, focusing particularly on the pathogenesis and epidemiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Physical and Chemical Mutagens and Xenobiotic Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how specific physical and chemical agents—including aflatoxin, UV radiation, polycyclic hydrocarbons, TCDD, and aromatic amines—cause DNA adducts and mutations through direct damage or xenobiotic metabolic activation.

topics.label: Tumor Initiation, Promotion, and Host Tissue Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the two-stage model of carcinogenesis, contrasting direct mutational initiation with promotional factors like inflammation, signaling pathway activation, and developmental life-stage vulnerabilities.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting, Testing, and Evaluating Carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the analytical and experimental strategies used to demonstrate carcinogenicity, including mutational signature analysis, population epidemiology, in vivo animal bioassays, and in vitro Ames testing.
